title: HCC and Immunotherapy: The Potential Predictive Role of Gut Microbiota and Future Therapeutic Strategies
content: During the last decade, a new therapeutic revolution has involved the management of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This is made possible thanks to the documented efficacy of immunotherapy for this disease. In addition, new evidence demonstrated the role of the gut-liver axis and gut microbiota in host homeostasis, tumor development, and response to therapies. In particular, intestinal dysbiosis can alter the tumor microenvironment leading to the activation of intracellular signalling pathways that promote carcinogenesis. The composition of gut microbiota proved to influence the immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) efficacy and drug toxicities. Therefore, this review aims to deepen knowledge about the immunomodulatory role of gut microbiota and its possible employment as diagnostic and predictive biomarkers in diagnosis and response to immunotherapy of HCC, respectively.
